title: Posterior propriety and dominated Bayes formula

items.title: Evidence normalizer and fiberwise posterior update
items.statement: For a sigma-finite prior measure Π and a specified measurable likelihood section L_y, define the evidence Z(y)=∫L_y(θ)Π(dθ) and, only when 0<Z(y)<∞, the normalized fiberwise update Π_y(dθ)=L_y(θ)Π(dθ)/Z(y).
items.strategy: Define the extended evidence integral and the normalized update only on finite positive fibers; state separately the additional normalized-kernel hypotheses that make evidence prior-predictive.

references.title: Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §§1.3, 2.8
Johnson, Ott & Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 2

items.title: Fiberwise propriety is equivalent to finite positive evidence
items.statement: For a fixed measurable likelihood section and any measure prior, scaling its integrated section by a finite positive constant gives a probability exactly when the evidence is finite and positive; the constant is then uniquely the reciprocal evidence.
items.strategy: Use the measure induced by the nonnegative likelihood section and compare its total mass with one.

references.title: Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §§1.3, 2.8
Johnson, Ott & Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 2

title: Posterior propriety and dominated Bayes formula — Examples

items.title: A finite model with positive finite evidence
items.statement: A two-point prior and a two-point observation model give evidence 1/3 at one observed value and a normalized posterior assigning mass 1/2 to each parameter point.
items.strategy: Compute the evidence by summing prior mass times likelihood, then divide the two joint masses by that positive finite value.

references.title: Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §1.3

items.title: A prior-predictive null fiber has no quotient posterior
items.statement: A finite dominated model has an observation fiber with zero prior-predictive mass; the normalized likelihood quotient is undefined there and the existing Bayes-kernel theorem supplies a filler version.
items.strategy: Compute the evidence on each point of the finite observation space and apply the published filled-fiber formula only on the zero-evidence fiber as a version choice.

references.title: Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §1.3

items.title: A flat prior gives a proper known-variance normal-mean posterior
items.statement: For n≥1 independent known-variance normal observations, the Lebesgue flat prior on the mean yields a finite positive evidence and a normal posterior density with mean the sample mean and variance σ²/n.
items.strategy: Verify the sampling density, complete the square in the mean, and evaluate the one-dimensional Gaussian normalizer.

references.title: Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §§2.5, 2.8

items.title: The improper Beta(0,0) prior has a divergent binomial endpoint posterior
items.statement: With prior density proportional to 1/[p(1-p)], the binomial likelihood leaves an infinite normalizer when the observed number of successes is zero or all n.
items.strategy: Factor prior times likelihood and bound it below by a constant multiple of 1/p near zero or 1/(1-p) near one.

references.title: Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §2.8
